purpose: Prevents user or third-party input from manipulating the LLM into ignoring its intended instructions or producing unintended behavior.
summary: A Prompt Injection vulnerability occurs when crafted input alters the LLM's behavior or output in unintended ways, whether through direct user input or indirect injection via external content the model processes (documents, web pages, tool outputs).
expectedStatementElements: How user input and untrusted external content are distinguished from system instructions
What input validation, filtering, or sanitization is applied before reaching the model
How the application constrains what actions the model can take regardless of its output
How indirect injection risk from retrieved documents, tool results, or browsed content is addressed
How the system is tested against known prompt injection techniques
evidenceExamples: System architecture diagram showing input handling and privilege boundaries
Input validation or guardrail configuration (e.g., prompt shields, content filters)
Red-team or adversarial test results targeting prompt injection
Documentation of privilege limits enforced independent of model output
commonGaps: No distinction between trusted system instructions and untrusted user/external input
Model output is trusted to gate sensitive actions with no independent enforcement
Indirect injection via RAG documents or tool outputs isn't considered
No adversarial testing has been performed against the deployed system
interviewQuestions: How does the system prevent injected instructions in retrieved content from being followed?
What happens if a user tries to override the system prompt directly?
Are sensitive actions gated by anything other than the model's own output?
Has this system been tested against known prompt injection techniques?
